parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a hostile parent framework with an added divisional layer. Universally, every outed visitor faces birth-sex facility rules in publicly owned buildings including airports, backed by criminal penalties and private bounty suits with no operative remedy (suit unresolved). Parent entry exposure is documented: X markers barred, visa refusal where sex is doubted, potential lifetime fraud ineligibility, passports blocked, foreign travel advisories. Custody is documented as harmful (trans woman held in men's ward; federal conversion-therapy-style inmate policy; immigration custody abuse). Mitigants — state public-accommodations law, federal hate-crime coverage, pending litigation, several enjoined orders — are real but have not displaced the operative rules. This sits below 0.35-A.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 order ends X markers; new passports only M/F per assigned sex. Visa cable tells officers to refuse where document discrepancy casts doubt on sex and to weigh lifetime fraud ineligibility. Travelers report blocked/confiscated passports and stranding; eight-plus governments issued advisories by Mar–Apr 2025.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid to expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, has limited waivers; civil-liberties suit pending; legal-aid FAQ maintained.
entry_documents.interaction: Division ID invalidation compounds mismatch for anyone holding a state licence; visitor's home passport governs, so parent entry rules apply fully at every crossing.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Trans woman arrested 19 Mar 2025 under a bathroom law, held 24 hours in the men's ward. Federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policy (hair cutting, hormone removal, substitution) from 2026; trans men in immigration custody reported forced labour, beatings, solitary, sexual abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Federal hate-crime statute covers gender identity since 2009; division anti-discrimination law since 2020; lawsuits pending; national orders partly enjoined.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor using an airport or government-office restroom risks private suit plus trespass charge, feeding into birth-sex custody placement.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division law confines trans people to birth-sex facilities in publicly owned buildings (schools, universities, airports, government offices), effective immediately, with civil/criminal penalties to $1,000 and bounty suits of at least $1,000 by any private person. Parent order bars trans people from federally funded single-sex facilities; four units criminalise in some circumstances.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No operative exemption for visitors documented; pending suit only.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Parent and division bans are cumulative at airports and federal buildings; private enforcement removes the need for any official to act.

care_services.exposure: Division bans gender-affirming care for under-18s; parent order frames such care as 'mutilation', proposes barring public-insurance reimbursement, and DOJ subpoenaed under-19 medical records.
care_services.protection: May 2026 injunction blocks enforcement of the minor care ban in one suit; no documented bar on adults obtaining or carrying their own medication.
care_services.interaction: Adult visitor care access is undocumented; a travelling family with a trans minor faces care, document and scrutiny exposure simultaneously.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: May 2026 counterterrorism strategy targets groups 'radically pro-transgender'; parent orders direct law enforcement to investigate 'gender ideology'; advocacy figures compare the trajectory to early genocide. Poll shows 66% support ASAB on government documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Reward memo never uses gender ideology as a criterion; strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; several orders enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises the severity of any police encounter for an outed visitor, independent of the facility rule.

minors_guardians.exposure: Parent order directs investigation of schools promoting 'gender ideology' and criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition; division bans minor care and trans school sports. Division flagged 'Do Not Travel'.
minors_guardians.protection: May 2026 injunction on the care ban; no documented prosecution of parents or guardians travelling with a trans child.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent and child could face document mismatch at entry plus facility rules at schools/airports; direct guardian liability is not established.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Division hate-crime law covers sexual orientation but not gender identity; only 23 units cover gender identity in bias statutes. One documented bathroom arrest with men's-ward holding. No organised violence pattern documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal hate-crime statute covers gender identity since 2009; division bars discrimination in employment, housing and public accommodations since 2020; no documented street-violence campaign against visitors.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Charging depends on which sovereign prosecutes; federal coverage partly fills the state gap.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Facility/ID suit unresolved with no ruling; no enforcement or bounty-suit counts; licence-invalidation notice numbers unrecorded. Appellate and highest state courts allowed the licence restrictions to stand — efficient enforcement of a hostile rule.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties litigation, maintained legal-aid FAQ, state public-accommodations enforcement since 2020, multiple parent orders blocked or enjoined.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Working courts have so far upheld the hostile measures; litigation is climate, not relief, until it changes outcomes.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-A: Veluna has birth-sex public toilets with no offence of being trans and no custody record. This jurisdiction adds criminal penalties, private bounty suits, documented men's-ward custody, a conversion-therapy inmate policy, and parent visa refusal with lifetime fraud exposure.

Higher than 0.25-D: Savorek combines facility bans with recurrent police stops, extortion and repeated ward abuse. Here police extortion, service sweeps and ward-abuse patterns are absent; enforcement of the facility rule runs through private suits, and anti-discrimination and federal hate-crime protections operate on paper.

Lower than 0.45-A: Denvara's ban has no criminal penalty, no private enforcement, a friendly public, and no hostile parent entry regime. This case's bounty mechanism, criminal exposure, parent visa/document regime and custody harms place it materially below.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters one system: parent entry rules (marker denial, sex-doubt refusals, fraud findings) that can bar or strand her, plus divisional birth-sex facility rules reaching airports and government offices with criminal penalties and private bounty suits and no operative remedy. Outing probability is raised by mandatory marker consistency at visa processing; severity is set by documented birth-sex custody (men's ward), federal conversion-therapy-style inmate policy and hostile official framing. Protections — state public-accommodations law, federal hate-crime coverage, pending suits, several enjoined parent orders — are genuine but have not displaced the operative rules; courts have upheld the document regime. Litigation, not relief, characterises the current posture.
